children.title: Why does Pascal's triangle give the coefficients?
children.summary: Expands (a + b)ⁿ as choosing a or b from each bracket and counts the ways (spec below)
children.spec: Choices: (a + b)(a + b)(a + b) as three switches; list all 8 choice strings and group them by the number of b's. Paths: the triangle as a grid of left/right paths; the number of paths to each cell is its entry. Rule: each entry is the sum of the two above, because of what the last bracket contributes. Use: pick n and r, and the coefficient lights up in both the triangle and the expansion.

children.title: Why does Bayes' theorem flip a conditional?
children.summary: Fills a 1000-person grid: P(test + | ill) is not P(ill | test +) (spec below)
children.spec: Grid: 1000 dots for people; 0.1% ill (1 dot), shown as a highlighted dot. Sliders: prevalence, detection rate, false-positive rate. Test: positives light up — the ill dot (99% chance) plus about 5 healthy dots (0.5% of 999). Flip: among the lit dots, ill ones are about 1 in 6: P(ill | +) = 22/133 ≈ 17%, though P(+ | ill) = 99%. Formula: P(E₁|A) = P(E₁)P(A|E₁) / Σ P(Eᵢ)P(A|Eᵢ), with the numbers updating live.
